title: The Ice Fisher
text: An old woman sits on a stool by a hole in the ice, a line dropped into the black water and a lantern beside her. She has caught nothing in years, she says cheerfully, but today she might. The line is moving. Whatever is down there is very big.

options.label: Sit and fish with her a while; she seems so glad of the company.

outcomes.text: She hauls up something with too many eyes and shares it out. It tastes good; nobody asks what it was.
Something takes her line and pulls hard. When it breaks the surface, it is looking at you.

options.label: The wisest asks what she fishes for, so far out on the ice.

outcomes.text: Her husband, she says; he fell through in the war. She is sure he will bite one day. Nobody has the heart to tell her otherwise.

options.label: Move on before dark. The ice is no place to be at night.

outcomes.text: She waves without looking up, calling after you to keep your feet dry. The Leader fails to, and the cold seeps in through their boots.
